asrt:fusion.asrt:name: staff
asrt:fusion.asrt:observed: the group filed a coupling between these two layers and kept them apart, and under its own rostering it was right: an extra engineer on the rota delivered no features, because the two rosters were separate and a name on one could not appear on the other. This holding runs one roster. A name moves between delivery and the rota inside a fortnight, and has forty-one times this year. At this level they are fungible and therefore one layer, and the group's coupling has no upper counterpart: it is absorbed, not refuted. The case against this fusion is in the layer above: the parts disagree on `timeSlack`, so the fused figure is unsized, and some of this demand survives a queue while some of it is lost at once. That does not make them two layers; the roster decides what is one layer.

asrt:elimination.asrt:observed: the two queues were reconciled ticket by ticket across the year. An escalation that becomes delivery work is closed on one and opened on the other, never counted twice.

payroll checked across all three establishments; the two rota posts are the parent's own and appear on no member's headcount. Had the rota been seconded from delivery, this would be 2, and the fused nameplate 10 rather than 12.

asrt:fusion.asrt:observed:
the group could not join these two and was right not to: `compute-us` is billed per reserved card and `compute-pt` by the month, and 4.4 GPU and 545 GPU-hour cannot be added. It filed two one-part fusions under two names, which is what that shape is for, and stopped there because it had no way to say how one becomes the other.
This holding meters both in card-hours for its own capacity planning, and a card reserved in Texas and an hour bought in Lisbon serve the same inference queue: work moves between them within a day, so they hold no remainder independently and they are one layer.
This fusion also absorbs a filed coupling, and owes a reason for it. The group observed that US inference above the reserved eight cards is routed to the Lisbon reservation, so the Portuguese layer's clearance falls when the US layer's demand peaks, and filed it as a `pm:Coupling` between two layers it could not join. That observation is not evidence for this fusion: coupling and fungibility are separate questions, and the group filed the same coupling shape between `labour` and `shift-line`, which are not one layer. What makes these two one layer is the metering. The coupling does not survive as a coupling, and it does not vanish either: once the two are one layer, work moving between them can only show up as hours counted twice inside it, which is what an elimination removes.
What a reader can disagree with is the factor, not the fusion. A reserved card is available every hour of the month and a purchased hour is not, so whether eight cards really deliver [5376, 5760, 5952] usable card-hours is a claim about utilisation that this filing does not separate out. It is stated here, where it can be argued with, rather than worked silently in a spreadsheet.

asrt:elimination.asrt:observed: the Portuguese member bursts onto the US member's reserved cards at quarter end and is cross-charged for it. Both filings are right about their own demand and the group would count those hours twice: once as US cards drawn, once as Portuguese hours bought. The invoices give the size.
both reservation contracts were read end to end. They name different providers in different regions and there is no shared hardware to remove.

The demand was counted twice and the draw was not, which is why `against` exists. The Portuguese member asked for the burst hours and the US cards served them: two asks, one service. Removing the same figure from the draw would delete work that actually happened.
